title: He Turned Down a Raise to Dodge Taxes 😂
description:
Theo just turned down a $2,000 raise because it "pushes him into the 22% bracket" — he's sure ALL his income would now be taxed at 22%. Nora grabs the marker: tax brackets are buckets. Only the slice of income above the line pays the higher rate, so his raise adds about $400 of federal income tax and he keeps around $1,600.

Moving into a higher bracket never makes your whole paycheck taxed at the higher rate.

Did you used to think brackets worked Theo's way? Be honest 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration using 2026 US federal income tax brackets for a single filer (taxable income $50,000 → $52,000, i.e. after deductions). Ignores state and local income tax, Social Security/Medicare payroll tax, credits and benefit phase-outs. Source: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (2026 tax rate tables). This is not financial advice.
